question: Which institution had launched the project E-Shakti for the digitization of all members of self-help groups in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**NABARD.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **NABARD (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development)** launched the project** E-Shakti** for the digitization of all members of **self-help groups **in India.
 
• The project aimed to digitize the data of around **3 crore members** of Self Help Groups across the country.
 
• E-Shakti helped in creating a** comprehensive database** of all the members of SHGs which helped in tracking their **financial transactions **and also provided them with easy access to **credit facilities.**
 
• The project also aimed to improve the **efficiency of the SHGs** and make them more self-sustainable by providing them with necessary training and capacity building.
 
• Overall, E-Shakti played a crucial role in promoting **financial inclusion and empowering women** in rural areas through the SHG model.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **SIDBI (Small Industries Development Bank of India)** is a financial institution that focuses on providing financial assistance and support to small-scale industries. 

 
 
• **Working Capital Assistance, Term Loan Assistance, Foreign Currency Loan, Receivables Support, Equity Support, Energy Saving Scheme**, and other services are provided by SIDBI to the MSME sector.
 
 
 
• **SEBI (Securities and Exchange Board of India) **is a regulatory body that oversees the functioning of the securities market in India.
 
 
• It was created by the Indian government in **1992** to oversee the **securities market **and safeguard the interests of investors who buy securities.
 
 
 
• **IFCI** (Industrial Finance Corporation of India) is a financial institution that provides **long-term financial assistance** to medium and large-scale industries. 
 
 
• The Government of India established The Industrial Finance Corporation of India (IFCI) on **July 1, 1948 **by enacting the **IFC Act 1948.**
